title: Principality of Waldeck and Pyrmont
capsule: Waldeck and Pyrmont was a small German principality in the Sauerland, surviving the Napoleonic upheaval as a formally independent state that joined the Confederation of the Rhine in 1807. After 1815 the Congress of Vienna confirmed its sovereignty within the German Confederation, and in 1849 the two territories of Waldeck and Pyrmont were legally merged into a single principality. In 1867 the ruling house signed an administrative convention ceding control of justice, finances, and the military to Prussia, effective 1 January 1868, while retaining nominal sovereignty; in 1871 Waldeck and Pyrmont became a constituent state of the newly proclaimed German Empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well documented through imperial German administrative records and the German Confederation's formal membership lists; borders were small and stable across this period.
